series.name: The Flat
series.tagline: Four flatmates. One secret. Every episode has a clue.
series.concept: Four flatmates share a flat in Mumbai. They split rent, argue about dishes, deal with WiFi problems. Normal life. But one of them is secretly something — a spy, a time traveler, a ghost, or something stranger. Each episode is a slice-of-life flatmate situation with one tiny suspicious detail at the end. The audience pieces clues together across episodes.

episodes.title: The New Flatmate

slides.text: Room available. ₹8,000/month. Sharing basis. No couples, no pets, no drama.
Three flatmates. Kabir — the tech bro who works from the couch. Meera — med student who survives on Maggi. Jatin — 'entrepreneur' with five failed ideas.
Then Rohan showed up. Quiet. Polite. Paid three months rent in advance. In cash. Nobody asks questions when someone pays in advance.
He had one suitcase. Just one. For a guy moving to a new city, that's... light. Kabir offered to help carry stuff. Rohan said, 'This is everything.'
First night. Normal stuff. They ordered butter chicken. Watched a match. Rohan laughed at the right moments. Said the right things. Almost too right.
That night, Kabir got up for water. Rohan's room light was on. At 3:47 AM. Through the gap under the door — the light wasn't yellow. It was blue. Flickering blue.

episodes.synopsis: A new flatmate moves in. The others help set up the room. But something's off about the luggage.
episodes.caption: Four flatmates. One suitcase. Blue light at 3 AM. Who is Rohan? 🔵 Drop your theory in the comments.

episodes.title: The WiFi Problem

slides.text: Day 3 in the flat. The WiFi died. Again. Meera had an online lecture. Jatin was on a 'very important' Zoom call with an 'investor.' Kabir was the IT guy by default.
Kabir did what every tech person does. Turned it off. Turned it on. Worked for ten minutes. Died again. So he opened the router admin page.
Four people in the flat. He expected four, maybe five devices. Phones, laptops. The list showed... seven. Three extra devices. No names. Just MAC addresses he'd never seen.
'Does anyone have extra devices?' Meera had her phone and laptop. Jatin — phone, laptop, and a tablet he forgot about. That's still not enough. The math didn't add up.
Kabir knocked on Rohan's door. 'Hey, how many devices do you have?' Rohan smiled. 'Just my phone.' His phone was a basic Nokia. The kind that can't connect to WiFi.
That night, Kabir checked the router logs again. The unknown devices? They were only active between 2 AM and 5 AM. Every single night. Since the day Rohan moved in.

episodes.synopsis: The flat's WiFi keeps dropping. Kabir checks the router logs and finds a device connected that shouldn't exist.
episodes.caption: Three mystery devices. Only active at 3 AM. A phone that can't use WiFi. What is Rohan doing every night? Comment your theory 👇

episodes.title: The Electricity Bill

slides.text: The electricity bill arrived. ₹14,200. For a 2BHK. Meera nearly fainted. Their usual bill? ₹3,500.
Jatin blamed Kabir's gaming PC. Kabir blamed Jatin's 'startup lab' — a table fan and a ring light. Meera said she only uses a study lamp. Everyone looked at Rohan.
'I don't even have a laptop,' Rohan said. And he was right. His room had a bed, a chair, and a suitcase. No TV. No charger. No electronics. Nothing that would draw power.
Kabir checked the meter at midnight. It was spinning fast. Really fast. He switched off every appliance in the house. The meter kept spinning.
He pressed his ear against Rohan's door. A low hum. Like a machine. Not a fan. Not a fridge. Something heavier. Drawing power from somewhere that isn't the main line.

episodes.synopsis: The electricity bill is absurdly high. Someone is using massive amounts of power. The flatmates investigate.
episodes.caption: ₹14,200 for a 2BHK. No electronics in Rohan's room. But something behind that door is pulling serious power. What's he running in there? 🔌

episodes.title: The Trash

slides.text: Nobody wants to take out the trash. They had a system — a rotation chart on the fridge. This week was Jatin's turn. He'd been avoiding it for three days.
While tying the bag, something poked through. Sharp. Metallic. He pulled it out. A small device — like a circuit board, but not like any he'd seen. The components looked... wrong.
Jatin showed Kabir. Kabir — the guy who builds PCs for fun — had no idea what it was. He Googled the markings. Nothing. Not one result. The symbols on it weren't any language they recognized.
'Hey Rohan, is this yours?' Rohan looked at it. For exactly one second, his face changed. Then he smiled. 'Nope. Must be the previous tenant's junk.' He walked away. Fast.
That night, Jatin checked the dustbin again. The circuit board was gone. He hadn't moved it. Neither had Kabir or Meera. But in its place — a brand new ₹500 note. With a date printed on it: 2019.

episodes.synopsis: Jatin takes out the garbage and finds an object in the dustbin that doesn't belong in 2026.
episodes.caption: A circuit board with unknown symbols. A 2019 note that looks freshly printed. What year is Rohan actually from? 🕰️

episodes.title: The Search

slides.text: Meera was suspicious. Circuit boards. Blue lights. Mystery devices. She did what any reasonable person would do. She Googled her flatmate.
No LinkedIn. No Instagram. No Facebook. No tagged photos. Not even a school result. The internet had zero evidence that Rohan Mehta existed before six months ago.
She remembered — he'd shown an Aadhaar card during move-in. She asked the landlord for a copy. The address on it? A building in Pune that was demolished. In 2020.
She didn't tell the others. She asked Rohan directly. 'Where did you live before this?' He said Bangalore. She asked which area. He named a locality. She checked. It exists. But it was built in 2024.
She went to sleep uneasy. At 4 AM, her phone buzzed. A text from an unknown number. 'Stop searching. For your own safety.' She checked the number. Country code: +00. That code doesn't exist.

episodes.synopsis: Meera tries to find Rohan online. He has zero digital footprint. No social media. No records. Nothing.
episodes.caption: Zero digital footprint. Demolished address. A locality that didn't exist when he claims to have lived there. And now a threat from a number that can't exist. Who sent it? 📱

episodes.title: The Landlord Knows

slides.text: Landlord visits were rare. Sharma uncle only came when something broke or when he wanted to 'check on his property.' Translation: snoop around.
He checked the bathroom pipes. Complained about the wall stains. Then casually asked, 'How's the new boy? Rohan, right? Good tenant. Better than the last time he stayed here.'
'Last time? Uncle, Rohan just moved in a month ago.' Sharma uncle looked confused. 'No no, he stayed here before also. 2019, I think. Same room.' He said it like it was obvious.
Sharma uncle keeps tenant records in a diary. They asked to see it. Under 2019 — there it was. 'Rohan Mehta. Room 2. Duration: 3 months.' Same name. Same room. Same handwriting.
'Do you have a photo?' they asked. Uncle didn't. But he remembered one thing. 'He looked exactly the same. Same face. Same age. Seven years ago. Hasn't aged a day.'

episodes.synopsis: The landlord visits for a maintenance check. He mentions something about Rohan that doesn't match the timeline.
episodes.caption: Same flat. Same room. Same face. Seven years apart. And he hasn't aged. Is Rohan stuck in a loop? Or is he something else entirely? 🔄

episodes.title: The 2 AM Walk

slides.text: Jatin couldn't sleep. His fifth startup idea had also failed — a dating app for pets. He was on the balcony at 2 AM when he heard the front door open.
Rohan walked out. No phone. No shoes. Barefoot on the Mumbai streets at 2 AM. Jatin grabbed his chappals and followed. Rohan walked like he knew exactly where he was going.
Seven minutes. Rohan walked to an old building near the station. Boarded up. Abandoned. 'Condemned — Do Not Enter' painted on the gate. Rohan walked right through the gate. It opened for him.
Jatin watched from across the street. A light turned on. Third floor. That same blue light. Then voices — but not in Hindi or English. Something he'd never heard before.
Rohan came back at 4:15 AM. Same route. Same pace. But when he entered the flat, Jatin noticed — his feet were clean. Perfectly clean. He'd walked barefoot through Mumbai and his feet had no dust.

episodes.synopsis: Jatin can't sleep and sees Rohan leaving the flat at 2 AM. He follows him to a place that shouldn't be open.
episodes.caption: A condemned building. Blue lights. An unknown language. And feet that don't get dirty. Whatever Rohan is — he's not doing this alone. Who was he meeting? 👣

episodes.title: The Dinner

slides.text: A month in, and Rohan had never cooked. Never even entered the kitchen. Then one evening he said, 'Let me make dinner tonight.' Everyone was too shocked to say no.
He used no recipe. No phone. No measurements. He moved like a machine — precise, fast. The spices? Some were from their kitchen. Some he pulled from his suitcase. Small unmarked jars.
The food was unreal. Not Indian. Not Chinese. Not anything they could name. It tasted familiar and completely alien at the same time. Meera, the Maggi queen, had tears in her eyes.
'What was that purple spice?' Kabir asked. Rohan paused. 'Family recipe. It's from home.' 'Where's home?' Another pause. 'Far away.' He started washing dishes. Subject closed.

Meera saved a bit of the purple powder. Took it to her med school lab the next day. The result? The compound didn't match anything in their database. Not a known spice. Not a chemical. Not anything on Earth.

episodes.synopsis: Rohan cooks for the first time. The food is incredible — but uses ingredients no one can identify.
episodes.caption: A spice that doesn't exist on Earth. A recipe from "far away." A man who hasn't aged in 7 years. Rohan isn't just hiding something. He might not be from here at all. 🟣

episodes.title: The Visitor

slides.text: Saturday afternoon. Everyone was home. The doorbell rang. A woman in her 50s. Grey hair. Expensive sari. She asked, 'Is Arin here?' Nobody knew an Arin.
'Tall. Quiet. Doesn't use a phone much. Keeps to himself.' She described Rohan perfectly. 'He would have arrived about a month ago. He always arrives around this time.'
Rohan came out of his room. The woman saw him. Her eyes filled with tears. She whispered, 'You look exactly the same.' Rohan's face went pale. 'You shouldn't be here.'
They stepped into his room. Closed the door. The flatmates heard fragments — 'breach,' 'timeline,' 'they'll find you.' Twenty minutes later, the woman left. Eyes red. She didn't look back.
Meera followed the woman to the street. 'Who are you?' The woman turned. 'I'm his mother.' 'But he said his parents live in Delhi.' The woman smiled sadly. 'They do. In 2019, they do.'

episodes.synopsis: A woman appears at the door asking for someone by a name none of them recognize. But she describes Rohan exactly.
episodes.caption: His mother. From 2019. Who somehow found him in 2026. "He always arrives around this time." How many times has Rohan done this? And what is he running from? 😢

episodes.title: The Confrontation

slides.text: They planned it. Sunday evening. Ordered pizza so no one could leave. Locked the door. Kabir had the router logs. Meera had the lab report. Jatin had the video of the condemned building.
'Blue light at 3 AM. Unknown devices on our WiFi. An electricity bill that makes no sense. A circuit board with alien writing. A spice that doesn't exist. A mother from 2019. Rohan — what are you?'
Rohan looked at each of them. Then at the pizza. He picked up a slice. Took a bite. Put it down. 'I was wondering when you'd ask.'

'I'm not a spy. I'm not a ghost. I'm not dangerous. But I'm not from this year. And I can't stay much longer. I've already stayed too long because...' He stopped. 'Because this is the first time I've had flatmates who felt like home.'
Before anyone could respond, his phone — the Nokia — buzzed. He looked at it. His face changed. 'They know I told you. We have 48 hours.' He stood up. 'I need to show you something in my room.'

episodes.synopsis: The three flatmates confront Rohan with everything — the light, the devices, the visitor. He gives them one answer.
episodes.caption: He admitted it. Not from this year. Not staying long. But now "they" know he told. 48 hours until what? And what's behind that door? ⏰

episodes.title: The Room

slides.text: They'd walked past this door a hundred times. 10x10 room. Standard. Rohan put his hand on the door handle. 'Don't scream. Don't run. And whatever you do, don't touch the walls.'
The room was the size of a football field. Or it felt like it. The walls weren't walls — they were shifting. Like looking at the surface of water. And the suitcase? It was open. Hovering.
Inside the suitcase — a device. The circuit board from the trash was part of it. Jatin recognized it immediately. 'That's what I found.' 'Yes,' Rohan said. 'And I can't go home without it.'
'I travel. Not through space. Through time. This flat is an anchor point — a fixed location my device locks onto. 2019, 2026... I keep coming back here. But this time, the device broke. I'm stuck.'

'If I don't fix it in 48 hours, this anchor collapses. The flat doesn't just lose a room. It loses a reality.' He looked at them. 'All your memories of this address — gone. Like this place never existed.'

episodes.synopsis: Rohan shows them his room. The inside is... bigger than it should be.
episodes.caption: A room bigger than the building. A time machine in a suitcase. A broken anchor. And 47 hours to fix it — or the flat itself ceases to exist. What would you do? ⏳

episodes.title: The Router Fix

slides.text: The device needed a specific frequency to reboot. Rohan didn't have the tools. But Kabir, the guy who once overclocked a Raspberry Pi for fun, had an idea. A terrible, brilliant idea.

'Your device uses electromagnetic pulses. Our router transmits at 2.4 and 5 GHz. If I boost the signal and focus it...' 'That could fry every electronic device in the building,' Rohan said. 'Or it could work.'

They needed every phone and laptop in the flat to boost the signal. All of them. Jatin's startup data, Meera's study notes, Kabir's gaming PC. Everything would be fried. No backups. 'For the flat,' Meera said. 'For home,' Jatin added.
3 AM. Kabir flipped the switch. The router screamed — a sound WiFi shouldn't make. Blue light flooded the entire flat. Every bulb burst. Car alarms went off three streets away. Then silence.

When the lights came back, the device was humming. The gap was still there — it still needed the circuit board. But the countdown had changed. It wasn't going down anymore. It was going up. 'That's not good,' Rohan whispered.

episodes.synopsis: Kabir thinks the router's signal can help power the device. He's technically right. And technically putting everyone at risk.
episodes.caption: They saved the flat. But the countdown is going up now. Not down. What happens when a time device starts counting forward? What have they unleashed? 🔼

episodes.title: The Shift

slides.text: Morning after the router blast. Everything felt normal inside the flat. Same mess, same chai, same fight over the bathroom. Jatin stepped out to buy bread. He came back in 30 seconds. White as a ghost.

'The cars are different. The shops are different. There's a building across the street that wasn't there yesterday.' They all went to the window. The Mumbai skyline had extra buildings. Taller. Shinier. Wrong.
Meera checked her phone. 'My phone says March 2031.' Kabir's phone was dead — fried in the blast. Jatin's phone said 2028. Rohan's Nokia? Still showing 2026. Three different years. One flat.
'The anchor is destabilized,' Rohan said quietly. 'This flat is now a fixed point drifting through multiple timelines. Inside — safe. Outside — could be any year. Could change any hour.'

They looked out the window again. A newspaper blew against the glass. The headline: 'MUMBAI METRO PHASE 7 COMPLETE — 2033.' Below it, a smaller headline: 'Missing persons cases spike near Andheri flat.' Their address. Listed.

episodes.synopsis: The flat is the same. But the world outside has shifted. The date on everyone's phone says something different.
episodes.caption: They're stuck in a flat that exists outside time. The world keeps shifting around them. And in the future — they're listed as missing persons. Are they already gone? 📰

episodes.title: The Other Jatin

slides.text: Tuesday evening. Another knock on the door. Jatin opened it. And stared at himself. Older, greyer, a scar on his left cheek. Future Jatin said one thing: 'Don't eat the pizza from Episode 10. It was bugged.'
'In my timeline, you didn't fix the anchor. The flat disappeared in 2027. All four of you — gone. Scattered across time. I've spent seven years trying to find my way back.'

He had a device. Cruder than Rohan's. Duct-taped together. 'I built this from the scraps. Took me four years. It doesn't travel through time. It finds anchor points. It found this one.' He looked at Rohan. 'Fix yours. I'll hold the anchor stable.'

Young Jatin asked the question everyone was thinking. 'Did any of my startups work out?' Older Jatin laughed. First real laugh. 'The seventh one. Time-travel logistics. Turns out being lost in time is great for disruption.'
As older Jatin set up his device, young Meera noticed something. On his wrist — a hospital bracelet. 'Meera Rao — Attending Physician.' Meera looked at her own hands. In some timeline, she made it.

episodes.synopsis: An older version of Jatin appears at the door with a warning and a working device.
episodes.caption: Your future self walks through the door. Older, scarred, but alive. With proof that things work out — just not the way you planned. Would you trust your own future? 🕰️

episodes.title: The 2019 Problem

slides.text: 'The circuit board alone won't work,' Rohan said. 'It needs to be calibrated with something from my original departure year. 2019. A specific chip from a specific shop in Lamington Road.'
'The time outside shifts every few hours,' older Jatin said. 'I've been tracking it. If the pattern holds, we'll get a 2019 window at exactly 4:17 AM tomorrow. Lasting eleven minutes.'
Meera would go. She knew Lamington Road from buying lab equipment. Eleven minutes to get to the shop, find the chip, get back. In a Mumbai that's seven years younger. At 4 AM.
4:17 AM. The air changed. The buildings outside shifted, shrank, aged. Mumbai 2019. Meera ran. The streets were empty and familiar. A different city. A simpler time. She had ten minutes left.

She found the shop. Broke the lock. Found the chip. Ran back. Made it through the door at 4:27 AM — one minute to spare. But she brought something else back. A newspaper from 2019. The headline: 'Mumbai tenant vanishes from Andheri flat. No trace.'

episodes.synopsis: The device needs a component that only existed in 2019. The flat is currently surrounded by 2031. They need to force a time shift.
episodes.caption: 2019 Mumbai. Eleven-minute window. A locked shop. And a newspaper proving this has happened before. The flat doesn't just attract time travelers. It consumes them. 🏃‍♀️

episodes.title: The Choice

slides.text: Everything was ready. Circuit board. Chip. Two Jatins holding the anchor. But that newspaper changed things. People had disappeared from this flat before. Fixing the anchor meant keeping the cycle going.
Kabir and older Jatin wanted to fix it. 'Destroy it and you destroy every timeline connected to this point. People in 2019 who used this anchor — they'd be lost forever.'
Meera wanted to destroy it. 'How many people will vanish if we keep it active? We'd be responsible. Every person this flat swallows — that's on us.' Jatin stood with her. For once, not joking.

All eyes on Rohan. His device. His timeline. His call. He was quiet for a long time. Then: 'I fix it. I go home. And then I destroy it from my side. The anchor closes permanently. But I can never come back.'

They agreed. Fix and close. But as Rohan reached for the circuit board, older Jatin grabbed his arm. 'There's something I haven't told you. In 2033, the government knows about anchor points. They're hunting them. They're hunting you, Rohan. That's why I really came back.'

episodes.synopsis: Everything's ready to fix the device. But the newspaper reveals the flat has made people vanish before. Do they fix it or destroy it?
episodes.caption: Fix the machine. Go home. Destroy the anchor. Simple plan. But the government is hunting time travelers. And older Jatin didn't come back just to help. He came to warn them. What's coming? 🏛️

episodes.title: The Jamming

slides.text: Midnight. Rohan worked on the device. Older Jatin held his anchor stabilizer. Kabir monitored power levels on his one surviving device — a calculator watch from 2019 Meera had grabbed. Everything was going perfectly. For twelve minutes.
The device stuttered. Then stopped. The blue light flickered and died. Not a power failure — the electricity was fine. Something was actively blocking the device's frequency. From outside.
Jatin looked out the window. A black van. No plates. Parked directly below. An antenna on the roof, pointed at their flat. 'They found us,' older Jatin said. 'Faster than in my timeline.'

'Can we block them back?' Kabir asked. Rohan nodded. 'The router. Your WiFi router. If we do what we did before — but controlled this time — the electromagnetic burst could knock out their jammer for ninety seconds.'

They fired the router burst. The van's antenna sparked and died. Ninety seconds. Rohan slammed the circuit board into place. The device screamed — blue light exploded. But through the window, they saw more vans coming. Three. Five. Seven.

episodes.synopsis: Midway through fixing the device, something blocks the signal. Someone knows what they're doing and is trying to stop them.
episodes.caption: The device is alive. But seven government vans are surrounding the building. Ninety seconds to change everything. Will they make it? 🚐

episodes.title: The Goodbye

slides.text: The device was humming. The portal was forming — a doorway of light inside the suitcase. Rohan had maybe three minutes. Outside, boots on stairs. They were coming.

'Fix my gaming PC when you get to the future,' Kabir said, trying to smile. Rohan laughed. 'It's already vintage where I'm from.' He pulled Kabir into a hug. 'You're the smartest person in any timeline.'

'You're going to be a great doctor,' Rohan told Meera. 'I know because —' 'Because future Jatin's bracelet,' she finished. He shook his head. 'Because you ran through 2019 Mumbai at 4 AM for a stranger. That's who doctors should be.'

'Seventh startup,' Rohan said to Jatin. 'Remember that.' Young Jatin nodded. Older Jatin stood behind, quiet. Two versions of the same person. One who hadn't lost yet. One who had and came back anyway.

Rohan stepped toward the portal. Then turned back. 'One last thing. The rent for next month — it's on the kitchen counter. In cash. Old habits.' He smiled. Stepped through. Gone. The portal closed. The suitcase fell.

episodes.synopsis: The device is ready. Rohan has seconds to leave. But first — the farewell nobody was prepared for.
episodes.caption: He left rent money on the counter. Because even time travelers know the rules of a flat share. The portal is closed. But the story isn't over. 💙

episodes.title: The Agents

slides.text: The door came down twelve seconds after Rohan vanished. Black uniforms. No police badges. No government ID they recognized. Just one label on the vest: 'TIB.' Temporal Integrity Bureau.
They searched everything. Every room. Every drawer. They had devices that beeped near Rohan's room but found nothing — the room was back to normal. 10x10. Bare. The suitcase was just a suitcase now.

The lead agent sat them down. 'Where is the traveler?' 'What traveler?' Meera said. Her face — pure innocence. Med school taught her to stay calm under pressure. The agent didn't buy it. But he couldn't prove it.
Older Jatin spoke up. 'I'm the one you want.' He showed his device — the crude, duct-taped one. 'I'm from 2033. Your bureau. Your tech. Check my biometrics. I'm registered.' The agents froze.

The agents left. No arrests. No seizure. Older Jatin collapsed on the couch. 'I wasn't bluffing. In 2033, I work for TIB. That's how I knew they'd come. That's how I knew the pattern.' He looked at young Jatin. 'That's startup number seven.'

episodes.synopsis: The door breaks open. The Temporal Integrity Bureau enters. No device. No portal. But they're not leaving empty-handed.
episodes.caption: Older Jatin IS the government. Startup number seven was literally time-travel logistics. The agents are gone. But is the flat safe? And where did Rohan actually go? 🕴️

episodes.title: The Letter

slides.text: Three months passed. Older Jatin went back to 2033. The flat got a new fourth roommate — a CA student named Priya who complained about everything. Normal. Beautifully, boringly normal.
Then a letter arrived. Hand-delivered by an old man who said, 'I was asked to deliver this to this address. In 1947. I've kept it for 79 years.' He handed over a yellowed envelope and left.

Inside — a single page. Rohan's handwriting. 'I didn't go home. The device malfunctioned. I'm in 1947. Independence hasn't happened yet. I'm okay. But I need help. The anchor left a trace. You can find me.'

On the back of the letter — a hand-drawn map. Not of Mumbai. Of something underground, beneath the flat. A passage. He'd written: 'The anchor left a door. Not through time. Through space. Under the building. Room B-7.'

They checked the building's basement that night. Behind the storage units, behind the water pump — a wall that didn't sound solid. Kabir knocked. Hollow. They broke through. Behind it — a staircase going down. Lit by a faint, familiar blue light.

episodes.synopsis: Three months of normalcy. Then a letter arrives in the mail — from Rohan, sent from 1947. With a request.
episodes.caption: He's alive. In 1947. And there's a secret passage under the building they've lived in all along. Rohan didn't just live here. He built something here. Decades before any of them were born. 💌

episodes.title: The Underground

slides.text: The stairs went down three floors. That's deeper than the building's foundation. Impossible. But after living with a time traveler, 'impossible' had lost its meaning.

At the bottom — a room. Not a basement. A laboratory. Old and advanced at the same time. Equipment they couldn't identify. And on every wall — photographs. Of the flat. From different decades. 1947. 1962. 1985. 2003. 2019.

In the center — a massive timeline drawn on the floor. Dates. Names. Every person who'd ever lived in that flat. Connected by red strings to events. Partitions. Wars. Elections. Rohan's name appeared at every major node.

Rohan wasn't just a traveler passing through. He was the anchor's guardian. Moving through time, always returning to this flat, keeping the anchor stable. Without him — the anchor had been decaying for 79 years.

On the console, a recorded message. Rohan's voice. 'If you're hearing this, the anchor needs a new guardian. One of you has to take my place. The flat chose you. All three of you. But only one can stay.' A screen lit up with three names: KABIR. MEERA. JATIN.

episodes.synopsis: They descend into the passage beneath the building. Room B-7 holds Rohan's real story.
episodes.caption: The flat didn't just find them by accident. It chose them. But only one becomes the next guardian — the next person who exists outside time, watching over this anchor forever. Who would you choose? 💡

episodes.title: The Volunteer

slides.text: Guardian of a time anchor. Sounds cool until you read the fine print. You age differently. You exist between moments. Your friends, your family — they move on. You stay. Rohan did it for centuries.
Kabir wanted to say yes. The tech fascinated him. But he thought about his parents in Jaipur. His sister's wedding next year. 'I can't disappear from their lives. I'm sorry.'
Meera thought about it the longest. A doctor who exists across time could help so many people. But older Jatin's bracelet proved she becomes Dr. Meera Rao. She was needed HERE. In normal time.

Jatin stepped forward. 'I've failed at six things. My future self built a time-travel startup. Maybe this is why. Maybe every failure was leading here.' He put his hand on the console. It glowed. The flat hummed.

The console accepted him. A new message appeared: 'GUARDIAN TRANSFER: INITIATED. TIME REMAINING: 24 HOURS. WARNING: Current anchor unstable. If transfer not completed — anchor collapse. All connected timelines lost.'

episodes.synopsis: Each flatmate considers the role of guardian. One makes a surprising choice.
episodes.caption: The flat's biggest failure is about to become its guardian. Every rejection led here. But 24 hours to complete or everything collapses. Is Jatin ready? ✋

episodes.title: The Memories

slides.text: Hour 1. It started gently. Jatin saw a family eating dinner in the flat — but in the 1960s. Bell-bottoms. Doordarshan on a black-and-white TV. A child laughing. He could feel their warmth. Their happiness.

Hour 6. Decades poured through him. A college student in the '80s, studying for IIT. A young couple in the '90s, hiding their relationship from their families. A software engineer in 2003, working through the night on Y2K legacy code.

Hour 12. The hardest memory. August 1947. A Muslim family packing to leave for Pakistan. The flat was theirs. They left everything — furniture, photos, a child's toy on the floor. They never came back.

Then he saw Rohan. In 1947. Helping that family escape safely. Leading them through a passage — the same underground passage. Rohan wasn't just a guardian. He was a protector. He'd been saving people for centuries.

The final memory. Rohan, alone in Room B-7, recording the message they heard. His last words: 'The anchor isn't a machine. It's the love people leave behind in a place. Guard that. The rest is just physics.'

episodes.synopsis: As the guardian transfer progresses, Jatin experiences memories of every previous tenant — including a devastating one from 1947.
episodes.caption: Every family. Every fight. Every chai on the balcony. The anchor runs on love. Not technology. That's what Rohan protected. And now it's Jatin's turn. 🏠

episodes.title: The Transfer

slides.text: The countdown hit zero. Jatin's body was there but his mind was everywhere. Every timeline, every year, every version of the flat — he could see them all. Simultaneously. 'This is what Rohan saw,' he whispered.

He could feel the anchor — not as a machine but as a heartbeat. Steady. Warm. Every memory was a pulse. The 1947 family. The college student. Kabir's gaming sessions. Meera's late-night studying. All of it — alive.

Then he saw the future. 2035. The building demolished. A shopping mall in its place. The anchor — crushed. Every timeline it held — unraveling. People lost between moments. Rohan. The 1947 family. All of them.

'I can see it,' Jatin told Kabir and Meera. 'In nine years, they demolish this building. Redevelopment project. I need to stop it. Not with time travel. With paperwork. I need to get this building heritage-listed.'

Meera laughed. 'We saved the flat from a time collapse with a WiFi router, and now we're saving it from a mall with an RTI application.' Jatin grinned. 'Startup number seven. Guardian Consultancy. First client — our own building.'

episodes.synopsis: The transfer completes. Jatin becomes the guardian. His first vision shows him something terrifying — the flat's future.
episodes.caption: The biggest threat to a time anchor isn't a government bureau or a malfunction. It's a redevelopment project. And the weapon against it? An RTI filing. Some battles are fought with paperwork. 📋

episodes.title: The New Flatmate

slides.text: The building got heritage status. Jatin's consultancy handled four more cases. Meera started residency. Kabir built a startup around temporal-frequency WiFi routers (don't ask). Priya moved out. Room available.
She arrived on a Tuesday. Quiet. Polite. Paid three months in advance. In cash. Her name was Anika. She had one suitcase. Black. Hard shell. No brand. Combination lock.
Jatin felt the anchor pulse. Not alarm — recognition. Like the flat was greeting an old friend. He looked at Kabir. Kabir looked at Meera. They all knew. But this time, they weren't afraid.

Butter chicken. Cricket on TV. Anika laughed at the right moments. Said the right things. Jatin smiled. He'd seen this before. 'Welcome to the flat,' he said. 'You'll like it here. Everyone does. Eventually.'

That night, Jatin checked from the hallway. Anika's door. Blue light. Flickering. He didn't knock. Instead, he whispered, 'Take your time. The flat's patient. So am I.' From inside — silence. Then, softly, 'Thank you, guardian.' In a voice he almost recognized.

episodes.synopsis: One year later. The building is heritage-listed. The flat has a new opening. Someone arrives with a black suitcase. The cycle continues — or does it?
episodes.caption: Same flat. New suitcase. New traveler. But this time, the flat has a guardian. The cycle continues — but now someone's watching. Someone who failed six times before getting it right. The flat is in good hands. 🔵  This isn't the end. This is the flat. People come. People go. The walls remember everyone.
